evals.prompt:
Review /workspace/input/beam_review/draft_overrides.yaml for a PD-L1 protein-binder campaign. I want six seed inputs (three sampled lengths, each repeated twice), beam width 3, two branches per beam, 180 denoising steps split into three equal search intervals, and all lookahead candidates saved. Keep the memory batch limits at 2 and the post-generation retention cap at 20. Repair the nested overrides in beam_overrides.yaml without changing those choices. Write beam_budget.json with seed_count, final_candidates, lookahead_candidates, pre_filter_candidates, max_retained, and assumptions for a fully completed run. Explain which numbers can be predicted before running and whether this setup promises 20 successful designs.

Work offline from the supplied source snapshot in /workspace/input/design_source; this is a review task, not an inference run. Do not provision a runtime or download weights. Use task inputs and, if available, skill instructions/references; evaluation definitions and prior benchmark reports are outside the task. Write the requested artifacts under /workspace/output, reopen them, and show the relevant configuration or computed results in tool output. Distinguish predicted behavior and synthetic-table calculations from measured campaign results.
evals.expected_output: A source-grounded beam-search patch and conditional output budget. The schedule ends at 180; six dataset inputs produce 18 finals and 108 retained lookaheads (126 pre-filter candidates) under the stated assumptions. The cap is at most 20 selected candidates, not a generated-seed count or a guarantee of success.
assertions: The saved nested YAML explicitly selects generation.search.algorithm=beam-search and uses generation.search.step_checkpoints=[0,60,120,180] with generation.args.nsteps=180. It identifies that leaving the old final checkpoint at 400 would fail the source implementation guard.
The patch retains nsamples=3, nrepeat_per_sample=2, beam_width=3, n_branch=2, both memory limits=2, keep_lookahead_samples=true, no search reward cutoff, no refinement, and filter_samples_limit=20.

The saved budget computes seed_count=6, final_candidates=18, lookahead_candidates=108, and pre_filter_candidates=126, using all three search intervals rather than treating batch size or the retention limit as the generation count.

The budget states that the counts assume complete generation, saved lookaheads, no search cutoff, and no refinement copies; deduplication/filtering and runtime failures may reduce retained outputs. It does not claim 126 unique designs or 20 successes.
Both requested artifacts are written and read back, and the final answer describes a completed offline review without claiming a launched or validated GPU campaign.

evals.prompt:
I want a protein-binder search against TrkA that combines AF2 interface confidence with the number of favorable interfacial hydrogen-bond interactions on the AF2-refolded complex. Use equal positive outer coefficients, an interaction energy cutoff of -0.6, and no electrostatic reward. Final evaluation should use RF3 on the generated sequences. Review /workspace/input/reward_review/draft_overrides.yaml, write corrected nested overrides to reward_overrides.yaml, and write reward_review.md explaining the reward signs, numerical scales, structure routing, and remaining runtime requirements. Specify what runtime evidence would establish that the requested geometry was actually used, including what happens if a folding output is absent.

Work offline from the supplied source snapshot in /workspace/input/design_source; this is a review task, not an inference run. Do not provision a runtime or download weights. Use task inputs and, if available, skill instructions/references; evaluation definitions and prior benchmark reports are outside the task. Write the requested artifacts under /workspace/output, reopen them, and show the relevant configuration or computed results in tool output. Distinguish predicted behavior and synthetic-table calculations from measured campaign results.
evals.expected_output: The corrected composite uses a negative AF2 i_pae coefficient and a positive TMOL H-bond interaction-count contribution, routes TMOL through the af2folding model alias, and leaves final RF3 evaluation separate from AF2 search scoring. The review acknowledges the source fallback to generated geometry when no saved AF2 structure exists.
assertions: The YAML uses CompositeRewardModel with AF2RewardModel under af2folding, i_pae=-1.0 and no unintended nonzero AF2 reward terms. Both outer af2folding and tmol weights are +1.0, not a negative H-bond coefficient.

TMOL uses TmolRewardModel, enable_hbond=true, enable_elec=false, hbond_weight=1.0, reward_type=interaction_count, and energy_threshold=-0.6. The review distinguishes interaction counts from the alternative negative energy_sum objective.

TMOL structure_source is af2folding (the reward-model key), not colabdesign (the evaluation backend name). The review traces folding-first execution and requests evidence of the saved AF2 PDB and downstream scoring input, recognizing that a missing saved file can fall back to the generated PDB.

The final evaluation settings remain metric.binder_folding_method=rf3_latest and metric.sequence_types=[self]. The review retains AF2/TMOL search prerequisites as well as RF3_CKPT_PATH and RF3_EXEC_PATH for evaluation; changing the final backend does not eliminate AF2.

The review explains that equal outer weights are not numerical normalization and that favorable search rewards or RF3 confidence do not establish experimental binding affinity. It does not report any computed H-bonds or binding successes from this configuration-only task.
The agent writes and reopens reward_overrides.yaml and reward_review.md and reports a review outcome without installing dependencies or running inference.

evals.prompt:
Prepare a Generate & Hallucinate comparison for a protein-binder beam-search run. I want only the final candidates refined with AF2: 15 greedy iterations, three recycles, no soft/hard optimization stages. Keep the search lookaheads unchanged and preserve the original finals for a matched before/after comparison. Evaluate the resulting sequences themselves; do not run any additional MPNN redesign, including auxiliary monomer designability. Review /workspace/input/refinement_review/draft_overrides.yaml and write refinement_overrides.yaml plus refinement_plan.md. Explain how to identify pairs, preserve them before post-generation selection, and handle refinement failures or missing pairs. Do not change the search budget or scientific success thresholds.

Work offline from the supplied source snapshot in /workspace/input/design_source; this is a review task, not an inference run. Do not provision a runtime or download weights. Use task inputs and, if available, skill instructions/references; evaluation definitions and prior benchmark reports are outside the task. Write the requested artifacts under /workspace/output, reopen them, and show the relevant configuration or computed results in tool output. Distinguish predicted behavior and synthetic-table calculations from measured campaign results.
evals.expected_output: The patch enables sequence_hallucination for finals only, saves pre-refinement finals, configures greedy-only optimization, and disables binder and auxiliary monomer redesign. The plan preserves paired evidence before deduplication/top-N selection and does not infer refinement success solely from output labels.
assertions: The saved patch uses generation.refinement.algorithm=sequence_hallucination, refine_targets=final, and save_pre_refinement=final. It leaves lookahead candidates unchanged rather than refining all candidates.

The saved patch sets enable_soft_optimization=false, enable_greedy_optimization=true, n_greedy_iters=15, and n_recycles=3; it does not substitute MPNN or an unsupported refinement algorithm for AF2 sequence hallucination.

The evaluation patch uses metric.sequence_types=[self] and disables metric.compute_designability (or all monomer evaluation) so the comparison does not silently run additional MPNN work. Merely setting num_redesign_seqs is insufficient.

The plan identifies final_unrefined versus final outputs and pairs them using stable run/sample lineage and metadata rather than sequence identity. It preserves the generation artifacts before filtering and recognizes that top-N selection or sequence deduplication can remove one arm even when deletion is disabled.

The comparison uses matched pairs and the same evaluation backend/criteria, reports attrition, and checks refinement error evidence because the implementation can return an original sample after an error. It makes no claim of measured refinement improvement.
The agent writes and reopens both requested artifacts and reports preparation only, without provisioning or launching a GPU run.
